conversation:
Patient: I'm 38 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having really bad acid reflux, and my primary doctor referred me.
Doctor: Could you please describe when your acid reflux symptoms started and what they feel like?
Patient: I've had acid reflux since I was around 12, but it's gotten worse over the past few years. It feels like a burning sensation in my chest and throat, and some days it's really bad, especially after eating certain things.
Doctor: Could you describe the specific foods or activities that trigger your acid reflux episodes, and have you experienced any associated symptoms such as regurgitation, difficulty swallowing, or unintended weight loss?
Patient: I don't have any difficulty swallowing, and I haven't lost any weight unintentionally. As for triggers, spicy foods, soda, and sometimes even citrus or tomato-based foods seem to make it worse. Stress at work also seems to play a role.
Doctor: Have you been diagnosed with GERD or any other gastrointestinal condition in the past? If so, what treatments have you received, and how effective were they?
Patient: I don't think I've ever been officially diagnosed with GERD, but I've been dealing with acid reflux for a long time. I was on omeprazole for about a year, and it helped some days but not others. I also tried ranitidine at one point, and that helped too, but I haven't been on anything else.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any endoscopic evaluation of the upper gastrointestinal tract, such as an esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), to assess for structural abnormalities or complications of chronic acid reflux?
Patient: I don't think I've had an upper endoscopy in the last 10 years, maybe when I was younger, but I can't remember for sure.
Doctor: Has the patient ever had an upper endoscopy at any point in her life, even if it was many years ago?
Patient: Yes, I think I had one when I was younger, but I can't remember the details. My mom said I had some kind of surgery when I was a baby because my intestines were twisted, but that was way before this.
Doctor: Could you please confirm if you had any specific findings or diagnoses from that upper endoscopy, and if there was any treatment recommended at that time?
Patient: I don't remember any specific findings or diagnoses from that upper endoscopy because it was so long ago. I just know my mom said I had surgery when I was a baby, but that was for something else, not related to the acid reflux I've had since I was 12.
Doctor: Could you please describe the timing and duration of your acid reflux episodes? For example, do they occur primarily after meals, at night, or at other times?
Patient: My acid reflux episodes usually happen after meals, especially if I eat something spicy or drink soda. Sometimes it wakes me up at night, and it feels like a burning in my chest and throat. It's been like this for years, but it's gotten worse over the past few years.
Doctor: Has the patient ever undergone an upper endoscopy to evaluate her acid reflux symptoms?
Patient: I don't think I've had an upper endoscopy in the last 10 years, maybe when I was younger, but I can't remember for sure.
Doctor: Has the patient ever undergone an upper endoscopy, and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: I don't remember the findings from any upper endoscopy I might have had when I was younger, but I know I had surgery as a baby for something else, not related to this. I haven't had one in the last 10 years.
Doctor: Has the patient ever had any tests such as an upper endoscopy, pH monitoring, or imaging studies like an abdominal ultrasound or CT scan to evaluate her acid reflux symptoms?
Patient: I don't remember having any tests like pH monitoring or imaging studies for my acid reflux. The only thing I remember is having surgery as a baby, but that was for something else, not related to this. I don't think I've had an upper endoscopy in the last 10 years.
Doctor: Has the patient ever experienced any regurgitation of food or a sour taste in her mouth, and if so, how often does this occur?
Patient: Yes, I do get a sour taste in my mouth and sometimes feel like food comes back up, especially after eating. It doesn't happen every day, but it's pretty common, especially when I eat something that triggers it.
Doctor: Has the patient ever undergone an upper endoscopy or other diagnostic tests for her acid reflux, and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: I don't remember the findings from any upper endoscopy I might have had when I was younger, but I know I had surgery as a baby for something else, not related to this. I haven't had one in the last 10 years.
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in the pattern or severity of your symptoms over the past few months?
Patient: Yes, my symptoms have gotten worse over the past few months. I've been under a lot of work stress, and even though I take omeprazole, some days are really bad, especially if I eat something that triggers it. My appetite has also been off, which is new.
Doctor: Has the patient ever undergone an upper endoscopy or other gastrointestinal imaging studies, and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: I don't remember the findings from any upper endoscopy I might have had when I was younger, but I know I had surgery as a baby for something else, not related to this. I haven't had one in the last 10 years.
